title: Arthur
about: A playboy millionaire must choose between his fortune and the working-class woman he loves.
cue: Serve dessert when Hobson says something devastatingly dry.
faces: "I'm Arthur, I'm rich, and I'm having a lovely time. Hobson, bring the car around, and bring a sandwich."

    StartersSusan Johnson engagement canapésRye squares with smoked salmon, lemon crème fraîche and dillHow to make it6 slices of rye bread30g butter, softened200g smoked salmon100ml crème fraîche1 lemon, zested1 small bunch dillcracked black pepper, to tasteButter the rye slices and cut each into small squares.Whip the crème fraîche with the lemon zest until it holds a soft peak.Top each square with smoked salmon, a small dot of crème fraîche, a dill sprig and cracked pepper.Caviar bliniWarm buckwheat blini, crème fraîche, salmon roe and snipped chivesHow to make it16 buckwheat blinis150ml crème fraîche1 small jar salmon roe1 small bunch chivesWarm the blini on a tray in a 180°C oven.Top each with a teaspoon of crème fraîche, a little roe and snipped chives.Serve straight away on a silver tray if you have one.Hobson's cucumber and cress sandwichesHobson the butler, keeping Arthur's world properly civilisedHow to make itAs written, serves 4Crustless white bread with herbed cream cheese, paper-thin cucumber and peppery cress, cut into neat fingers.Peel and very thinly slice 1 telegraph cucumber, salt lightly for 10 minutes and pat dry.Beat 150g cream cheese with 2 tbsp chopped dill, lemon zest and pepper.Spread over 12 slices white bread.Top 6 with cucumber and a punnet of cress, close with the rest and press gently.Cut off the crusts and slice into 4 fingers each.Chicken liver pâté with toasted briocheHobson would call it adequate, then finish it.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsHobson's Sunday roast beefTopside roasted rare to medium rare, with gravy from the pan juicesHow to make it1.5kg beef topside2 tbsp olive oil3 eggs150g plain flour300ml milk400ml beef stock2 tbsp vegetable oil, for the tinssalt and pepper, to tasteHeat the oven to 200°C. Rub the beef with oil, salt and pepper.Whisk the eggs, flour and milk into a smooth batter and leave to rest.Roast the beef until the centre reads 52°C on a probe.Rest the beef under foil. Raise the oven to 220°C, heat the oiled tins until smoking, pour in the batter and bake the puddings until risen and golden.Make gravy by simmering the stock with the pan juices until slightly thickened. Carve and serve.Linda's diner ReubenLinda, the waitress who shoplifted a tieHow to make itAs written, serves 4Corned beef, Swiss and sauerkraut on rye with Russian dressing, fried in butter until crisp and melting.Mix 80g mayonnaise, 2 tbsp tomato sauce, 1 tsp horseradish and 1 tbsp chopped gherkin for the dressing.Butter 8 slices rye on one side.On the unbuttered side spread dressing, then layer 400g sliced corned beef, 200g drained sauerkraut and 8 slices Swiss.Close and fry over medium heat for 4 minutes a side, pressing down, until crisp and melted.SweetsCrème brûléeVanilla bean custard baked in ramekins under a crackly sugar crustHow to make it600ml thickened cream1 vanilla bean6 egg yolks80g caster sugar, for the custard4 tbsp caster sugar, for the topHeat the oven to 150°C. Warm the cream with the split vanilla bean until steaming.Whisk the yolks and sugar, then pour the cream over, whisking gently. Strain into ramekins.Stand the ramekins in a tray of hot water and bake until just set with a wobble.Cool, then chill overnight. Chilling counts toward the cooking time.Sprinkle with sugar and torch to amber.DrinksArthur's Kir royaleChampagne poured over a splash of crème de cassisHow to make it60ml creme de cassis480ml brut champagne, chilled4 raspberriesChill the flutes in the freezer.Pour the cassis into each glass, tilt and top slowly with champagne so it does not foam over.Drop a raspberry into each glass and serve straight away.Single malt and sodaArthur's usual, Hobson pouring with a sigh.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
